architecture.decision: The user chose 'rebuild as one web-hub' over (a) merging just NovelForge+MediaForge in customtkinter or (b) a bare launcher. Reason: AI Studio was already a fast FastAPI + web-frontend app, while customtkinter itself was identified as a real source of the sluggishness in the other two.
architecture.shape: The hub is a thin orchestrator. Each tool keeps its OWN FastAPI backend running as its own subprocess on its own port. The hub window (GTK3 + WebKit2) loads a static shell via file:// and iframes whichever backend is active. Closing the hub window SIGTERMs all backends.
architecture.why_iframes: AI Studio already had a complete working frontend, so an iframe let it join with zero changes. NovelForge and MediaForge had no web frontend at all, so theirs were written fresh - also iframed for consistency. A future pass could inline all three into one shared-DOM page; iframes were the low-risk way to get everything under one roof.
architecture.backend_discovery: app_window.py's BACKENDS list defines each backend (name, root dir, module target, port, src_dir). A backend whose .venv/bin/python or src_dir is missing is skipped at launch and the sidebar shows a placeholder instead of a broken iframe. Availability is written to /home/ejb/Forge/static/status.json at startup and read by the shell's JS.

the_porting_pattern.summary: Used identically for both NovelForge and MediaForge. Follow it for anything new.
the_porting_pattern.step_1: Leave every business-logic module COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED. None of them ever imported customtkinter - they were already cleanly separated behind plain callback hooks (log / progress / stream / on_status / on_line / should_stop). This is why the port was feasible at all.
the_porting_pattern.step_2: web_app.py (FastAPI) per app imports those modules directly and exposes them as REST endpoints.
the_porting_pattern.step_3: For long-running work, use the generic Job class already defined in each web_app.py: a background thread + a queue.Queue of events, drained by an SSE endpoint at /api/jobs/{id}/events that BATCHES events in ~120ms windows before sending. THIS BATCHING IS THE ACTUAL FIX for the original sluggishness - the old customtkinter apps did one Tk textbox insert per streamed token; the SSE endpoint coalesces bursts into single messages.
the_porting_pattern.step_4: static/index.html per app is the frontend, sharing a dark CSS-token system (--bg/--panel/--border/--text/--muted/--accent) so all three look like one product.
the_porting_pattern.critical_sse_rule: ONE EventSource per job. Job events go through a queue.Queue, which is single-consumer (NOT broadcast) - opening two connections to the same job silently splits events between them. A bug of exactly this kind was caught and fixed in NovelForge's audiobook panel. If a panel needs both log text and progress, pass both callbacks into ONE stream helper (see streamJobGeneric in NovelForge's index.html).
the_porting_pattern.job_result_convention: Jobs that produce a result set job.result inside their work function; GET /api/jobs/{id} returns it (MediaForge) or a dedicated /result endpoint returns it (some NovelForge/MediaForge routes). MediaForge's GET /api/jobs/{id} includes 'result' generically - prefer that for anything new.

bug_fixes_requested_by_user.bug: AI Studio: images come out with misplaced squares / weird blocks
bug_fixes_requested_by_user.root_cause: The Iris Xe's Vulkan driver enforces a per-allocation VRAM ceiling. Above ~768px the UNet/VAE im2col buffers exceed it; ggml then silently reroutes individual ops to CPU one node at a time (this is exactly the 'alternating CPU then iGPU bursts, then it times out' behaviour the user described), and partially-written buffers produce coherent rectangular block artifacts. Confirmed from ggml_vulkan OOM warnings in outputs/sd-server-gpu.log at 896x896 and 1024x1024.
bug_fixes_requested_by_user.fix: Added --diffusion-conv-direct --vae-conv-direct --vae-tiling to the sd-server launch in src/model_manager.py. conv-direct swaps im2col for a much smaller-footprint direct conv; vae-tiling caps decode memory.
bug_fixes_requested_by_user.verified: NO - the user explicitly asked to skip the live high-res verification test and check it themselves through the real app. THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST UNVERIFIED CLAIM IN THE PROJECT. If they report artifacts still happening, next levers are --max-vram with graph-cut segmented execution, or a hard UI resolution cap.
